audits.title: 1971 Five years of the National Audit of Inpatient Falls
audits.standard: NICE guidelines/quality standards for multifactorial falls risk assessment and safe post-fall management
audits.setting: National Audit of Inpatient Falls, all hospitals in England and Wales (inpatient femoral fractures from National Hip Fracture Database)

cycle1.result: Checked for injury before moving from floor 69%; flat lifting equipment 22%; medical assessment within 30 mins of fall 52%.

audits.intervention: Continuous national audit with improvement resources and activities.

cycle2.result: Checked for injury before moving 77%; flat lifting equipment 29%; medical assessment within 30 mins 60%.

audits.other_findings: Around 2000 inpatient femoral fractures a year; these patients have double the 30-day mortality of those who fracture elsewhere. Most aspects of MFRA improved.
audits.citation: Whitney J, Sheshi N. 1971 Five years of the National Audit of Inpatient Falls. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad246.071.

audits.title: An Audit Of Post Fall Medical Reviews In Older Hospital Inpatients
audits.standard: National 'Service User Falls: A Practical Guide for Review' and NICE CT head criteria
audits.setting: Large university teaching hospital, St James's Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 27% had a CT brain; 3/49 (6%) met NICE criteria but did not have CT.

audits.intervention: Post-fall review pro forma/checklist and CT brain decision tool planned; re-audit planned.
audits.other_findings: Many reviews omitted important history and examination details.
audits.citation: Carroll T, Daly S, Briggs R. An Audit Of Post Fall Medical Reviews In Older Hospital Inpatients. Age and Ageing. 2024;53(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afae178.184.

audits.title: Prevention and Management of Falls in Older Adults admitted to Woodlands Hospital, an inpatient Old Age Psychiatric Unit
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on the management of falls in older people
audits.setting: Woodlands Hospital, inpatient old age psychiatric unit

cycle1.result: 100% had individualised interventions; 97.3% had falls risk assessment on admission; 60.3% checked for signs of fracture; 78.3% had physical examination within 12 hours; 75% had neurological observations.

audits.other_findings: Weekly MDT falls risk review, fracture checks and neurological examination need improvement; re-audit planned for September 2021.
audits.citation: Darod N. Prevention and Management of Falls in Older Adults admitted to Woodlands Hospital, an inpatient Old Age Psychiatric Unit. Eur Psychiatry. 2022;65(Suppl 1):S174-S175.

audits.title: The National Falls and Bone Health Audit: implications for UK emergency care.
audits.standard: National standards/indicators for integrated falls services developed by a multidisciplinary group
audits.setting: Emergency departments and minor injury units; National Clinical Audit of Falls and Bone Health (Royal College of Physicians)

cycle1.result: Management of falls and bone health in older people remained suboptimal in emergency departments and minor injury units; opportunities for evidence-based risk assessment and management were missed (no figures in abstract).

audits.other_findings: Falls account for 700,000 emergency department visits and 4 million bed days a year in England.
audits.citation: Banerjee J, Benger J, Treml J, Martin FC, Grant R, Lowe D, et al.. The National Falls and Bone Health Audit: implications for UK emergency care. Emerg Med J. 2012;29(10):830-832. doi:10.1136/emermed-2011-200501. PMID: 22045604.

audits.title: Accurate falls risk assessment and interventions for preventing falls in patients in the acute care setting within a private hospital in a large capital city: a best practice implementation project.
audits.standard: Hospital Falls Minimization Program and National Safety and Quality Health Service Standard 10 (Preventing Falls and Harm from Falls); eight JBI audit criteria
audits.setting: Calvary Wakefield Hospital, private acute hospital, medical and surgical wards

cycle1.result: Baseline audit showed significant opportunity for improvement in all criteria (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Corrective action plan after the baseline audit (details not given in abstract).

cycle2.period: Six months after the implementation phase
cycle2.result: Results were maintained and consistent with the first follow-up audit (figures not given in abstract).

audits.other_findings: At the first follow-up (three months), nearly all criteria improved; formal staff education improved by 46% and patient and family education by 43%.
audits.citation: Szymaniak S. Accurate falls risk assessment and interventions for preventing falls in patients in the acute care setting within a private hospital in a large capital city: a best practice implementation project. JBI Database System Rev Implement Rep. 2015;13(9):386-406. doi:10.11124/jbisrir-2015-2089. PMID: 26470676.

audits.title: Clinical Audit as a Quality Improvement Tool in Measurements of Lying and Standing Blood Pressure for Elderly Patients Admitted With a Hip Fracture.
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on falls in older people: lying and standing blood pressure measurement; RCP FFAP guidance on LSBP procedure
audits.setting: Orthopaedics department (ethical approval from Salisbury District Hospital)

cycle1.result: LSBP measured in 16 (32%); correctly documented in 12/16 (75%).

audits.intervention: Results presented at geriatric medicine mortality meeting with root cause analysis; flyers and posters on wards, teaching sessions for ward staff on LSBP measurement and recording on POET, and aide-memoires placed around wards.

cycle2.result: LSBP measured in 45 (83.3%) (p < 0.0001); correctly documented in 45 (100%) (p = 0.0035).

audits.other_findings: Root cause analysis found insufficient staff training and need for assistance to stand patients post-operatively.
audits.citation: Okereke IC, Mmerem K, Aly M. Clinical Audit as a Quality Improvement Tool in Measurements of Lying and Standing Blood Pressure for Elderly Patients Admitted With a Hip Fracture. Cureus. 2021;13(7):e16781. doi:10.7759/cureus.16781. PMID: 34513388.

audits.title: Improving Orthostatic Hypotension Screening in Fall Prevention: A Two-Cycle Audit on Falls Assessment and Lying and Standing Blood Pressure Measurement.
audits.standard: NICE falls guidance: completion of falls assessment and lying and standing blood pressure measurement; target 100%
audits.setting: Orthopaedic rehabilitation ward, district general hospital in North East England

cycle1.result: Falls assessment completed 38/41 (93%); lying and standing BP recorded 14/41 (34%).

audits.intervention: Cycle 1 results presented at departmental teaching, daily reminders at the morning huddle, educational flyers and targeted education for doctors, nurses and healthcare staff.

cycle2.result: Falls assessment completed 40/41 (98%) (p = 0.61); lying and standing BP recorded 28/41 (68%) (p = 0.004).

audits.other_findings: Systolic drop of 20 mmHg or more found in 5/14 (36%) then 13/28 (46.4%) of those measured. LSBP was sometimes marked as completed in the falls assessment when it was not done.
audits.citation: Yusuf Y, Alfardan N, Matar E, Najeeb F, Abdulmotaleb Z. Improving Orthostatic Hypotension Screening in Fall Prevention: A Two-Cycle Audit on Falls Assessment and Lying and Standing Blood Pressure Measurement. Cureus. 2025;17(3):e81138. doi:10.7759/cureus.81138. PMID: 40276417.

audits.title: Reducing unwarranted variation in medication reviews following a fall: a closed-loop audit in primary care.
audits.standard: NICE CG161/NG5 and NHS England guidance: documented medication review within 4 weeks after a fall; target 100%
audits.setting: UK GP surgery (Mid and South Essex)
audits.intervention: Clinician education on NICE guidance, SystmOne prompts and weekly MDT fall reviews.
audits.other_findings: More appropriate deprescribing, particularly of benzodiazepines, anticholinergics and antihypertensives.
audits.citation: Khan H. Reducing unwarranted variation in medication reviews following a fall: a closed-loop audit in primary care. Br J Gen Pract. 2026;76(suppl 1):bjgp26X745449. doi:10.3399/bjgp26x745449. PMID: 42134925.

audits.title: 61 AUDIT: MEDICATION REVIEW POST INPATIENT FALLS
audits.standard: HSE Service User Falls guide; British Society guideline Medicines and Falls in Hospital; STOPP/START; NICE Falls in Older People 2013
audits.setting: Mater Misericordiae University Hospital, Dublin; inpatient falls with serious injury

cycle1.result: Medication review carried out after the fall in 9.09% (3); 84.85% had polypharmacy; no falls-risk medications stopped or dose changed.

audits.other_findings: Post-fall reviews mainly by interns (48.49%) and SHOs (39.39%); 51.52% on antihypertensives and 24.24% on sedatives.
audits.citation: Gibbons C, Gaynor E, Duggan J, Blackstock J, Mullen M, Keena A, et al.. 61 AUDIT: MEDICATION REVIEW POST INPATIENT FALLS. Age and Ageing. 2021;50(Supplement_3):ii9-ii41. doi:10.1093/ageing/afab219.61.

audits.title: 985 A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT ON CALL BELL IN REACH IN AN ACUTE OLDER PERSON MEDICINE WARD (AGE > 85 YEARS)
audits.standard: National Inpatient Falls Audit: call bell within reach; target 95% or more
audits.setting: Acute older person medicine ward (age over 85), Queen Alexandra Hospital, Portsmouth
audits.intervention: Four PDSA changes: stickers in notes, teaching for nurses, a video in a closed ward social group, and a safety huddle and handover reminder

cycle2.result: Call bell in reach 93.88% after the 4th PDSA cycle, sustained.

audits.other_findings: Data were from 10 beds; reminders at huddle and handover were the most effective change, and no correlation with falls was shown.
audits.citation: Noor M, Islam M, Spice C. 985 A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT ON CALL BELL IN REACH IN AN ACUTE OLDER PERSON MEDICINE WARD (AGE > 85 YEARS). Age and Ageing. 2022;51(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/ageing/afac126.038.

audits.setting: Medical admissions, St Vincent's University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Fall description 91.7%; syncope asked 50%; previous falls 33.3%; cardiac exam 96.7%; neuro exam 71.1%; mobility baseline 41.7%; medication review 60%; mobility assessed under 72 hours 41.6%; differential for the fall 76.7%.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit of Staff Compliance With Local, National & International Guidelines Regarding Falls Assessment in The Geriatric Emergency Medicine Unit
audits.standard: 11-standard audit tool based on the World Guidelines for Falls Prevention and Management (2022) and ESC syncope guidelines (2018)
audits.setting: Geriatric Emergency Medicine Unit, University Hospital Limerick

cycle1.result: Compliance ranged 15-100% across 11 standards; composite compliance 65%; careful history 55%; ECG 60%; lying and standing BP 25%.

audits.intervention: Team-based education on assessment practices and a 'falls from a standing height checklist'.

cycle2.result: Composite compliance 90%; careful history 100%; ECG 90%; lying and standing BP 65%.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles: re-audits in Q2 2024 and Q1 2025.

audits.title: A Clinical Audit Of Current Assessment Of Falls In The Older Adult by the Pathfinder Service
audits.standard: 2022 World Guidelines for falls prevention and management; target 100% documentation of eight key assessments
audits.setting: Pathfinder service (National Ambulance Service and University Limerick Hospital Group), patients who fell at home without admission

cycle1.result: Falls risk stratification 12.5%; other domains not given individually.

audits.intervention: Eight practice changes aligned with the World Falls Guidelines (delirium screen, lying/standing BP, ECG, standardised balance and gait, ADL and environmental assessments, risk stratification, 3 key questions).

cycle2.result: Implementation increased by 34% to 71% on average; 3 key questions increased by 72%; falls risk stratification 79%; standardised mobility assessment compliance doubled.

audits.other_findings: Further improvements being embedded in team education and patient information.
audits.citation: Richardson E, O'Brien C, Gaumont D, Ruane P, O'Connor D, Donohue N. A Clinical Audit Of Current Assessment Of Falls In The Older Adult by the Pathfinder Service. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_4). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf318.095.

audits.title: eP514 General Surgical Inpatient Falls: An Audit of Current Practices
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians national falls guidance and local protocol

cycle1.result: All assessed for falls risk within 24 hours of admission; all falls reviewed but local protocol fully followed in 10 (71%); 57% (8/14) further investigated.

audits.other_findings: Standard falls proforma not routinely used; one moderate harm and one death in a patient admitted with a fall who fell again.
audits.citation: Zhu L, George J, Hwang Z, Wilson T. eP514 General Surgical Inpatient Falls: An Audit of Current Practices. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.483.
